Participants, procedure and measures
Seventy-five boys aged 14–16 allocated rewards using matrices. The four conditions crossed being told about explicit groups with apparent similarity on prior preferences. The matrices distinguish own-group favoritism, fairness and total joint reward.

scope-01-result
result

scope-01
result
Result
Explicit categorization produced favoritism even when group membership was known to be arbitrary. Similarity also contributed, but more weakly. Fairness remained evident across conditions.
